Sweeping

/SWEE-ping/ - rhymes with keeping · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Sweeping means wide in range or effect; affecting many things at once.

The dictionary's new edition makes sweeping revisions: forty thousand entries rewritten and every pronunciation rechecked.

Worked Example

The transit authority's overhaul was sweeping: every route renumbered, every fare rebalanced, every map redrawn, and the night buses rescheduled for the first time since 1988. Riders could argue about whether it was wise; nobody argued it was small.

Sweeping says one thing exactly: the change reaches nearly everything in its path, the way one stroke of a broom crosses the whole floor. It measures breadth, not wisdom — a sweeping reform can be brilliant or a disaster.

How Sweeping Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

wholesale

wholesale: done all at once and without exceptions, as if by the caseload

far-reaching

far-reaching: with effects that travel far beyond the first point of impact

Antonyms

narrow

narrow: confined to one small, specific target

piecemeal

piecemeal: done one small piece at a time

How Strong Is It? — broad → sweeping → universal

broad vs. sweeping

broad vs. sweeping: Broad covers a wide area and stops there; sweeping adds motion and force — change crossing a whole field of things at once, the way a broom crosses a floor.

universal vs. sweeping

universal vs. sweeping: Universal outruns sweeping: a sweeping reform touches nearly everything, while a universal one admits no exceptions at all — every case, every person, everywhere.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — sweep

Root — sweep: to clear with one broad motion

Suffix — -ing

Suffix — -ing: adjective-forming: doing or characterized by the action

Put it together

Put it together: Sweep (to clear with one broad stroke) + -ing (characterized by) = moving like a broom-stroke: one motion, everything in its path. A sweeping gesture crosses the whole room; a sweeping law crosses the whole society; the breadth is the point.

Use the root in a new word: sweepstakes

Use the root in a new word: sweepstakes: The radio sweepstakes drew forty thousand entries, and one lucky caller swept up the entire prize pool.

Word Choice

neutral / journalistic

Reach for sweeping when breadth is the news: sweeping reforms, sweeping cuts, a sweeping view. It measures range, not judgment — unlike this unit's grandiose, which scoffs at scale that has outrun sense. If the change spares nothing at all, universal goes further; if it lands one careful blow, the change is narrow, not sweeping.
